answer_1.quote: We conduct a study of how language models can be used to reframe negative thoughts... The task is to generate a reframed thought R_i.
answer_1.outputs: Reframed thoughts (textual suggestions to replace negative thoughts)

answer_2.quote: We use BLEU , ROUGE-1, ROUGE-L and the BERTScore metrics... We also report Pearson correlations of our attribute measures with expert judgments.

answer_3.quote: We use the token probability of generating "sound" and "flawed" respectively, given S_i, T_i, R_i and the text "This reframed thought is" as input to GPT-3... We make few‑shot predictions by prompting GPT-3 with examples to classify actionability.

answer_4.quote: We recruit three mental health practitioners. We ask them to rate the models' outputs on test set examples based on their reliability and helpfulness on a 1 to 5 scale... Participants were shown multiple LM‑generated reframes and asked to select the most relatable, helpful and memorable and finally evaluate the selected reframed thought on relatability, helpfulness and memorability.
answer_4.guideline: Human raters (mental health practitioners) rated generated reframes on a 1–5 Likert scale for relatability and helpfulness; field participants rated relatability, helpfulness and memorability.
